intro.title: Upload a dataset in 4 steps
intro.body: First you describe your dataset, then you pick the template, upload your file and review the validation. Once submitted it goes into review: a database editor approves it before anyone else can see it.

intro.requiredNote: Only 4 items are required; the rest is optional and you can fill it in later.

columnHelp.attr:DEPTH_FROM_CM: Numeric top of the sampled depth range, in centimeters (e.g. 0 for a 0-20 cm sample). Equivalent to 'Min Depth' — use whichever your source file already provides, not both.
columnHelp.attr:DEPTH_TO_CM: Numeric bottom of the sampled depth range, in centimeters (e.g. 20 for a 0-20 cm sample). Equivalent to 'Max Depth'.
columnHelp.attr:DEPTH_MIN_CM: Same as 'Depth From' — the top of the range, in centimeters. Some sources label it 'min' instead of 'from'; use only one of the two per sample.
columnHelp.attr:DEPTH_MAX_CM: Same as 'Depth To' — the bottom of the range, in centimeters. Some sources label it 'max' instead of 'to'; use only one of the two per sample.
columnHelp.attr:DEPTH_TEXT: Depth exactly as written in the original file, for cases that don't fit a clean numeric range (e.g. 'Ah horizon' or '0-20/20-40 cm'). Prefer the numeric fields above when possible.
columnHelp.attr:HORIZON_CLASS: Soil horizon classification (e.g. A, B, C, O), for profile/horizon samples.
columnHelp.attr:HORIZON_CODE: Identifier code for the horizon within its profile (e.g. Ap1, Bt2).
columnHelp.attr:HORIZON_DESCRIPTION: Free-text description of the horizon (color, texture, structure, etc.).
columnHelp.attr:SAMPLE_ID_ORIGINAL_OBS: Original sample ID or field observation note, exactly as recorded in the source file.
columnHelp.attr:SAMPLING_METHOD: Method or tool used to collect the sample (e.g. auger, pit, core).

validation.errorsFound: Errors were found in the file
validation.reviewPending: A database editor will review your dataset. The data will be published once approved and we will email you.
validation.issuesGroupedHint: Grouped by column and problem type. Fix the column in your file and upload it again.

issues.INVALID_DATE: Invalid date. Use a specific date formatted as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2019-03-15); DD/MM/YYYY and DD-MM-YYYY also work. A range such as "March/April 2019" is not a date — use the sampling day for this row.
issues.NOT_NUMERIC: Not a number. Enter the number only (e.g. 12.5), with a dot or comma decimal separator. For results below the detection limit write "<LOQ", "<LOD" or "<0.5". If there is no value, leave the cell empty or write "NA".
issues.NOT_NUMERIC_latitude: Latitude is not a number. Use decimal degrees with a dot (e.g. 4.6097), not degrees and minutes.
issues.NOT_NUMERIC_longitude: Longitude is not a number. Use decimal degrees with a dot (e.g. -74.0817), not degrees and minutes.
issues.NOT_BOOLEAN: Value not recognised as Yes/No. Use "Yes"/"No", "true"/"false" or 1/0.
issues.OUT_OF_RANGE: Value outside the allowed range for this column.
issues.OUT_OF_RANGE_latitude: Latitude out of range. It must be between -90 and 90.
issues.OUT_OF_RANGE_longitude: Longitude out of range. It must be between -180 and 180.
issues.REQUIRED: This column is required and the row leaves it empty. Fill it in or remove the row.
issues.MISSING_COLUMN: A required column is missing from the file. Download the template again and copy your data into it.
issues.DUPLICATE: Duplicate sample within the file: another row has the same site, date and sample code. Keep only one.
issues.ALREADY_EXISTS: A value already exists for this sample in this column. Uploads only add new data, they never overwrite. Remove those rows from the file.
issues.POSSIBLE_SWAP: Latitude and longitude possibly swapped? Check the point lands where you expect.
issues.NEW_SAMPLE_TYPE: This sample type is not in the catalogue yet; it will be created when the upload is approved.
issues.UNKNOWN_COLUMN: Unrecognised column: it will be ignored. Use the template generated by the platform to avoid this.
issues.UNKNOWN_VARIABLE: The variable for this column does not exist in the catalogue.
issues.UNKNOWN_ATTRIBUTE: The attribute for this column does not exist in the catalogue.
issues.NEW_VARIABLE_INVALID_TYPE: Unrecognised value type in the “New variables” sheet. Use Number, Text, Date or Yes/No.
issues.NEW_VARIABLE_INVALID_MATRIX: Unrecognised matrix in the “New variables” sheet. Pick one from the dropdown.
issues.NEW_VARIABLE_DUPLICATE: This variable is described twice in the “New variables” sheet. Each name must be unique, because it is how its column is found.
issues.NEW_VARIABLE_INVALID_NAME: The variable name has no usable letters or digits.
issues.NEW_VARIABLE_LINKED: This variable already exists in the catalogue, so your column was linked to it (its name is shown).
issues.NEW_VARIABLE_SIMILAR: It looks like a variable that already exists (shown). The reviewer will decide whether to merge them instead of creating a new one.
issues.NEW_VARIABLE_UNIT_UNKNOWN: The unit is not in the catalogue; the reviewer will choose one.
issues.NEW_VARIABLE_UNUSED: This variable is described in “New variables”, but no column in “Template” has that header, so it will not be used.
issues.UNDEFINED_COLUMN: This column has no technical id and no description in “New variables”, so it was ignored. If it is a new variable, describe it in that sheet.

help.title: The name the dataset will be published and searched under. Descriptive, not an internal code.
help.abstract: Summary of what the dataset holds: what was measured, where, when and why. This is what a reader sees first.
help.keywords: Terms that help people find the dataset. Concepts from FAO's AGROVOC thesaurus are suggested; you can also add your own terms.
help.version: Version number of this dataset. Raise it when you publish a correction or an extension.
help.persistent_id: The dataset's DOI, if it was already published in TIP, Dataverse or similar. A permanent identifier such as 10.1234/zenodo.5678901. Leave empty if it has none yet: it is assigned on publication.
help.related_publications: DOIs of scientific papers that used this data. Not the dataset's own DOI, but the publications citing it.
help.temporal_coverage_start: Date of the earliest sampling this dataset covers.
help.temporal_coverage_end: Date of the latest sampling. Leave empty if the campaign is still running.
help.spatial_coverage: Geographic area the data covers: region, state or country.
help.spatial_data_type: Geometry the data describes. The platform stores sites as points today; pick another option if your dataset describes lines, polygons or a grid.
help.expected_matrices: Material analysed (soil, leaf, grain). Filled in automatically from your file.
help.expected_variables: Variables measured in the dataset. Filled in automatically from your file.
help.sampling_design: How sampling points were chosen: random, stratified, grid, number of replicates.
help.access_level: Who will be able to see the data: Public (any user), Restricted (named people only) or Private (you and the data team).
help.authorized_users: People allowed to see this restricted dataset. Whoever uploads it always keeps access.
help.embargo_until: Optional. Date from which this private or restricted dataset may be opened. Useful when a paper is on the way: it is shared once the article is out. Leave empty if no date is planned.
help.license: Legal terms for reuse. When in doubt, CC-BY-4.0: reuse is allowed with attribution. CC0 has no conditions; NC licenses forbid commercial use.
help.access_conditions: What someone must do to obtain the data: who to contact, whether an agreement is needed.
help.data_source: Centre or organisation responsible for the data. Start typing to see CGIAR centres.
help.provenance: Where the data comes from: project, campaign or original source.
help.methodology: Field and analytical methods used. Lets others judge whether the data is comparable.
help.citation: How the dataset should be cited. If it is already published, copy the official citation.
help.usage_notes: Warnings for interpreting the data correctly: limitations, assumptions, what not to do.
help.contact_name: Person to ask about this data.
help.contact_email: Contact address published alongside the dataset.
help.contact_name_2: Backup contact, in case the primary one doesn't answer.
help.authors: Authors of the dataset, for proper citation. Different from the contact: the contact is who to write to, the authors are who to cite.
help.funding_information: Funder and grant/project number, as one text (e.g. "INV-12345 — Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation").
help.language: Language the data and its documentation are in.
help.related_datasets: Other datasets this one relates to or continues — your own, on Dataverse, or on CGSpace.
help.subject: Discipline the dataset belongs to. Start typing for suggestions (the same vocabulary Dataverse uses); you can also type your own.
help.geographic_bounding_box: Geographic extent of the dataset. Filled in automatically when importing from Dataverse.

features.databaseBody: PostgreSQL with PostGIS to store all soil research project data in a unified and scalable way.
features.vizBody: Configurable charts and interactive dashboards to analyze soil, climate, and vegetation variables by project and site.

features.uploadBody: Easy import from Excel using customizable templates, with automatic data structure validation.
features.downloadBody: Download filtered data in standard formats (CSV, Excel) for external analysis and sharing with collaborators.
features.aiBody: Artificial intelligence to interpret soil data, generate insights, and answer questions about the results.
